props.title: The Adventures of Prince Achmed
props.initialSlug: First animated feature film: shadow puppet magic

sections.content: The Adventures of Prince Achmed revolutionized animation as the world's oldest surviving animated feature film. Lotte Reiniger crafted this masterpiece using intricate silhouette animation, cutting out detailed paper figures and photographing them frame-by-frame. The film adapts stories from "One Thousand and One Nights," following Prince Achmed's magical flying horse adventure, battles with sorcerers, and romance with Peri Banu. Its influence echoes through Fantasia (1940) and modern shadow-inspired works like The Prince of Egypt (1998) and Song of the Sea (2014).

sections.content: Reiniger's innovative techniques laid groundwork for generations of experimental animators. Her meticulous craftsmanship inspired direct descendants like Michel Ocelot's Princes and Princesses (2000) and Tales of the Night (2011), which explicitly pay homage to silhouette animation. The film's arabesque design elements and flowing movement patterns influenced Disney's Aladdin (1992) and Laika's Kubo and the Two Strings (2016). SUBHEAD: Early Animation Innovation and Legacy

While contemporaries like The Lost World (1925) experimented with stop-motion dinosaurs, Reiniger developed a wholly unique animation language. Her use of jointed paper figures and multiplane camera techniques predated Disney's innovations by over a decade. This technical mastery enabled fluid character movement that still impresses today, visible in the flying horse sequences that would later inspire works like How to Train Your Dragon (2010) and The Last Unicorn (1982).
